text: The Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy (2024-2025 Catalog) is offered by the School of Economic, Political and Policy Sciences (EPPS) at The University of Texas at Dallas. The degree plan consists of: Core Curriculum (42 semester credit hours); Major Core Courses (12 semester credit hours); Foreign Language Requirement (12 semester credit hours); International Political Economy Electives (24 semester credit hours); Area Electives (12 semester credit hours); and Elective Requirements (18 semester credit hours). A minimum of 120 total semester credit hours (SCH) and a minimum of 45 upper-level SCH are required to complete the degree. The minimum GPA requirement is 2.0 in the major and 2.0 overall. Incoming freshmen must enroll and complete requirements of EPPS 1110 Critical Issues in the Social Sciences (Freshman Seminar). This degree plan is a product of the School of EPPS and is not considered an official university degree plan. For detailed degree information and requirements visit The University of Texas at Dallas Undergraduate Catalog, http://catalog.utdallas.edu. To view your official record, please view your Degree Progress Report in Orion.

text: The Core Curriculum for the Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy (2024-2025 Catalog) requires 42 semester credit hours: Communication (two courses, chosen from the approved list); Mathematics (one course, chosen from the approved list); Life and Physical Sciences (two courses, chosen from the approved list); Language, Philosophy and Culture (one course, chosen from the approved list); Creative Arts (one course, chosen from the approved list); American History (two courses, chosen from the approved list); Government/Political Science: GOVT 2305 and GOVT 2306; Social and Behavioral Sciences: ECON 2301; Methods of Quantitative Analysis in the Social and Policy Sciences (chosen from the approved list); and Component Area Option: ECON 2302. ECON 2301 and ECON 2302 are required major preparatory courses that also fulfill a Core Curriculum requirement, and their semester credit hours are counted in the Core Curriculum. Curriculum requirements can be fulfilled by other approved courses from institutions of higher education; the courses listed are recommended as the most efficient way to satisfy both Core Curriculum and Major Requirements at UT Dallas.
source_title: Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy Degree Plan (2024-2025 Catalog)

text: The Major Core Courses for the Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy (2024-2025 Catalog) total 12 semester credit hours. Students choose 4 out of the following 8 courses: GEOG 3370 The Global Economy; IPEC 3349 World Resources and Development; IPEC 4301 Political Economy of Industrialized Countries; IPEC 4302 Political Economy of Developing Countries; IPEC 4377 Politics of International Finance; PSCI 4329 Global Politics; PSCI 4356 International Political Economy; and PSCI 4360 Political Economy of Multinational Corporations.
source_title: Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy Degree Plan (2024-2025 Catalog)
section_heading: Major Core Courses: 12 semester credit hours

text: The Foreign Language Requirement for the Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy (2024-2025 Catalog) is 12 semester credit hours of the same language. Students can petition the Program Head for exceptions. If the language credit is obtained without taking classes, twelve additional semester credit hours of Free Electives (upper-division or lower-division) can be taken by the student.
source_title: Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy Degree Plan (2024-2025 Catalog)
section_heading: Foreign Language Requirement: 12 semester credit hours

text: The Bachelor of Arts in International Political Economy (2024-2025 Catalog) includes three elective blocks. International Political Economy Electives require 24 semester credit hours and Area Electives require 12 semester credit hours; for the list of approved courses for both, see https://epps.utdallas.edu/current-students/undergraduate-advising/. Elective Requirements total 18 semester credit hours and may be satisfied with lower- and upper-division courses from any field of study.
